intended_object: The inclusion map from the full subposet of admissible layers L ≤ U ⊆ B whose lower endpoint satisfies L ≤ D into the poset of all admissible layers. The module docstring says this inclusion is the right adjoint of the lower-cut operation L ↦ L ⊓ D.
explanation:
`LowerBounded P B D` is the subtype `{x : AdmissibleLayer P B // x.lower ≤ D}`. `lowerInclusion` is `Subtype.val`, so it sends each bounded layer to the same layer and forgets only the proof that `x.lower ≤ D`. This is exactly the inclusion of a full subposet. The subtype inherits its order from the poset of layers, and the next lemma, `lowerInclusion_monotone` (proved by `fun _ _ h => h`), shows that the map preserves that order. The library uses the map as the right adjoint in a Galois connection with `lowerCut`, which matches the module docstring.

There is no generality issue: the definition only reuses the ambient setting of `AdmissibleLayer` (an abelian category, an object property `P`, a subobject `D`). The general notion is the inclusion of a subtype, and Mathlib's `Subtype.val` is precisely that; this definition just gives it a name in this setting. Mathlib has no specific counterpart for admissible layers.

One could also see the definition as a thin wrapper with little content of its own. But it does name a genuine mathematical map, the inclusion functor of a subposet, and formalizes it correctly, so the verdict is faithful.
